---
title: "A first model"
---

Fit a linear model to 32 cars, print the estimates, and predict fuel economy for cars that are not in the data.

The page runs with the [extension](installation.qmd) or the plain-PHP [polyfill](extension-or-polyfill.qmd). The data are [mtcars](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#mtcars): fuel consumption and design of 32 cars (1973–74 models) from *Motor Trend*. `mpg` is miles per US gallon, `wt` is weight in 1,000 lb, and `am` is the transmission (0 automatic, 1 manual).

## Data

The formula functions take named columns: an associative array of `column => list of values`, with every column the same length. A table object with `toModelData()` or `toColumns()`, such as a phibble `DataFrame`, is also accepted. This page reads the CSV file by URL with phibble (`composer require phpstats/phibble`).

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phit\{fit_ols, predict, summary, tidy};

$cars = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/mtcars.csv',
);
```

- Numeric values make a numeric column.
- Strings make a factor whose levels sort in byte order. `factor()` in a formula makes a numeric column a factor.
- [Model formulas](formulas.qmd#data) lists every accepted column type.

## Fit

```php
$fit = fit_ols('mpg ~ wt + factor(am)', $cars);
```

`mpg` is the response. `wt + factor(am)` adds a slope for weight and a treatment-coded indicator for manual transmission, with automatic (0) as the reference level. The intercept is included unless the formula removes it with `- 1` or `+ 0`.

## Read the result

`summary()` prints the fit in the layout of R's `print(summary(fit))`.

```php
echo summary($fit);
```

```
Linear model fit by least squares
Formula: mpg ~ wt + factor(am)

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) 37.32155    3.05464  12.218 5.84e-13
wt          -5.35281    0.78824  -6.791 1.87e-07
factor(am)1 -0.02362    1.54565  -0.015    0.988

Residual standard error: 3.098 on 29 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared: 0.7528, Adjusted R-squared: 0.7358
F-statistic: 44.17 on 2 and 29 DF, p-value: 1.579e-09
```

- The `wt` coefficient is the difference in miles per gallon associated with 1,000 lb more weight, among cars with the same transmission.
- The `factor(am)1` coefficient is the difference between manual and automatic cars of the same weight. It is close to zero (−0.02 mpg, p = 0.988).

`tidy()` returns the coefficient table as columns, which a `DataFrame` can hold.

```php
$coefficients = DataFrame::fromColumns(tidy($fit, confInt: true));
echo $coefficients, "\n";
```

```
# A tibble: 3 × 7
  term        estimate std_error statistic  p_value conf_low conf_high
  <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
1 (Intercept)  37.3        3.05    12.2    5.84e-13    31.1      43.6 
2 wt           -5.35       0.788   -6.79   1.87e- 7    -6.96     -3.74
3 factor(am)1  -0.0236     1.55    -0.0153 9.88e- 1    -3.18      3.14
```

The fit itself is a PHP array. Every per-coefficient list follows the order of `columns`.

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `columns`, `named` | Coefficient names, and a `name => coefficient` map |
| `coefficients`, `std_errors`, `t_statistics`, `p_values` | One value per column |
| `conf_int` | 95% intervals, `[lower, upper]` per column |
| `covariance` | The coefficient covariance matrix |
| `fitted`, `residuals` | One value per retained row |
| `r_squared`, `adj_r_squared`, `sigma`, `rss`, `log_likelihood`, `df_residual` | Fit statistics |
| `n_input`, `n_observations`, `n_dropped`, `retained_rows`, `dropped_rows` | Sample accounting |
| `diagnostics` | Solver, convergence, and warnings |

```php
echo json_encode($fit['diagnostics']), "\n";
```

```
{"converged":true,"solver":"scaled_svd","warnings":[]}
```

`fit_generalized_linear()`, `fit_mixed_gaussian()`, and `fit_mixed_logistic()` return the same naming and accounting keys with the statistics of their model, and `summary()` and `tidy()` take their results too. See [Linear and generalized linear models](models.qmd) and [Mixed models](mixed-models.qmd).

## Predict

`predict()` rebuilds the formula over new data. The response column is not needed, and factor levels are those the fit saw.

```php
$new = ['wt' => [2.5, 3.5], 'am' => [1, 0]];
$p = predict($fit, $new, interval: 'prediction');

echo DataFrame::fromColumns([
    'wt' => $new['wt'],
    'am' => $new['am'],
    'mpg' => $p['fit'],
    'lower' => $p['lower'],
    'upper' => $p['upper'],
]), "\n";
```

```
# A tibble: 2 × 5
     wt    am   mpg lower upper
  <dbl> <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
1   2.5     1  23.9  17.3  30.5
2   3.5     0  18.6  12.1  25.1
```

- `interval: 'prediction'` covers one new car's fuel economy. `interval: 'confidence'` covers the mean.
- A level the fit never saw, such as `am` 2, throws an exception with code 1001.
- [Prediction](formulas.qmd#prediction-predict) covers generalized linear and mixed-model predictions.

## Missing values

`null` and `NAN` are missing. By default, a row with a missing value in any column the formula uses is dropped, and the fit emits one `E_WARNING`. With `mpg` set to `null` in the third row, the warning reads:

```
Phit\fit_ols(): dropped 1 of 32 observations with missing values (listwise deletion)
```

- The result reports `n_observations` 31, `n_input` 32, and `dropped_rows` `[2]`.
- `diagnostics.warnings` records `listwise deletion removed 1 of 32 original rows`.
- `missing: 'raise'` rejects missing values. The call throws an `Exception` with code 1001 and the message `missing values found with missing='raise'`.

[Missing values](missing-data.qmd) defines which values count as missing and how rows are counted.

## Errors

Invalid input and failed fits throw a PHP `Exception`. `getCode()` gives the category, for example:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 1001 | Invalid input |
| 1002 | Mismatched lengths |
| 1004 | Rank-deficient design |
| 1006 | Nonconvergence |

The full table is in the [API conventions](contracts.qmd#v01-diagnostics-and-errors).
